findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "fetch_leads" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_shortlist, fetch_leads, get_campaign, list_pending_outreach, list_replies, list_next_steps, get_campaign_stats · Private data: create_shortlist, list_next_steps · Public sink: create_shortlist, fetch_leads, list_campaigns, send_outreach, list_replies, get_campaign_stats · Destructive: continue_campaign.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_shortlist, fetch_leads, get_campaign, list_pending_outreach, list_replies, list_next_steps, get_campaign_stats · Private data: create_shortlist, list_next_steps · Public sink: create_shortlist, fetch_leads, list_campaigns, send_outreach, list_replies, get_campaign_stats · Destructive: continue_campaign

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
